meta.msNote: Not released yet. Microsoft adds it about eight weeks after the exam leaves beta. This opens the cert page where it will appear.

cards.back: **Eligible:** the user must **activate** the role when needed (can require MFA, justification, approval, a ticket) and it expires after a set time. **Active:** the role is on without activation. PIM gives **just-in-time, time-bound, audited** privileged access.

**Microsoft Entra roles**, **Azure resource roles** (Owner, Contributor and others at any scope) and **PIM for Groups** (just-in-time membership or ownership). Pair it with **access reviews** to remove assignments nobody needs.

**Assignments** (users or workload/agent identities, target resources, conditions such as location, device platform, client app, sign-in risk, user risk) and **access controls**: **grant** (block, require MFA, authentication strength, compliant device) and **session** (sign-in frequency, app-enforced restrictions).

cards.front: How do you roll out a Conditional Access policy safely?
cards.back: Start in **report-only** mode and check the sign-in logs. **Exclude emergency (break-glass) accounts.** Use the **What If** tool to test who a policy hits.

**Passkeys (FIDO2)**, **Windows Hello for Business** and **certificate-based authentication**. Enforce them with a Conditional Access **authentication strength**. SMS and voice are the weakest methods.

**App registration:** the global **application object**, where you define the app (redirect URIs, API permissions, secrets or certificates). **Enterprise application:** the **service principal**, the app's local identity in a tenant, where you control sign-in, assignment and consent.
**Delegated:** the app acts **as the signed-in user**, limited by what that user can do. **Application:** the app acts **as itself** with no user, and always needs **admin consent**.

Limit **user consent** to verified publishers and low-risk permissions (or turn it off), and turn on the **admin consent workflow** so users can request approval. Review and revoke grants under Enterprise applications → Permissions.

**System-assigned:** tied to one resource and deleted with it. **User-assigned:** a standalone resource you can attach to **many** resources. Both remove secrets from code; grant them Azure RBAC roles.

cards.front: What does Key Vault store, and which tiers exist?
cards.back: **Secrets** (passwords, connection strings), **keys** (cryptographic keys) and **certificates**. **Standard** protects keys with software; **Premium** adds **HSM-protected keys**. **Managed HSM** is a separate single-tenant HSM service.

**Azure RBAC** (recommended): roles at vault, or even single-object scope. **Vault access policies** (legacy): per-vault permission lists. The **management plane** (create the vault, settings) and **data plane** (read secrets, use keys) are authorized separately.

cards.front: Key Vault data-plane RBAC roles to recognize?
cards.back: **Key Vault Administrator** (all data-plane), **Secrets Officer** (manage secrets), **Secrets User** (read secret values), **Crypto Officer** (manage keys), **Crypto User** (use keys), **Certificates Officer**, **Reader** (metadata only), **Purge Operator**.

On by default and **cannot be turned off**. Deleted vaults and objects stay recoverable for **7 to 90 days** (default 90); the period is set at creation and **cannot be changed**. A deleted name cannot be reused until it is purged or expires.

Optional, **off by default**. When on, **nobody, not even Microsoft**, can purge a deleted vault or object until the retention period ends, and it **cannot be disabled**. Required by services that use customer-managed keys.

Firewall: **disable public access** or allow **selected virtual networks and IP ranges**; use a **private endpoint** for private access. The **Allow trusted Microsoft services** exception lets named Azure services through the firewall. They still need permission to the data.

Set **expiration dates**. Keys support an **auto-rotation policy**. Certificates can **auto-renew** with an integrated CA. Secrets rotate with Event Grid 'near expiry' events and automation. Each object has **versions**.

cards.front: Secrets scanning with Defender CSPM, and Defender for Key Vault?
cards.back: **Defender CSPM agentless secrets scanning** finds plaintext secrets and keys on VMs and in cloud deployments, and shows them in recommendations and **attack paths**. **Defender for Key Vault** raises **alerts** on unusual or suspicious access to vaults.

**Built-in:** maintained by Microsoft (allowed locations, require HTTPS…). **Custom:** your own JSON rule with `if` and `then.effect`. Group either into an **initiative** and **assign** at management group, subscription or resource group, with exclusions and **exemptions**.

cards.front: Security standards in Defender for Cloud?
cards.back: The **Microsoft cloud security benchmark (MCSB)** is assigned by default and drives **recommendations** and **secure score**. Add **regulatory standards** (ISO 27001, PCI DSS, NIST…) and custom standards. Standards are built on **Azure Policy** initiatives.

Shows each standard's controls as passed or failed, based on the assessed resources. Adding standards beyond the default needs a **paid Defender plan**. You can download reports and Microsoft's audit attestations.

**Remediate** (often a Fix button), **exempt** a resource (waived or mitigated), **disable** a rule, or assign an **owner and due date** with governance rules. **Deny** and **Enforce** options stop new non-compliant resources.

**Actions** and **NotActions** (management plane), **DataActions** and **NotDataActions** (data plane), and **AssignableScopes** (where it can be assigned). NotActions subtracts from Actions; it is **not** a deny.
Built from Entra permissions (for example app registration management) and assigned tenant-wide or scoped to an object or administrative unit. They need **Microsoft Entra ID P1**.

Use **Access control (IAM)** to review assignments at each scope, **PIM** to make standing roles eligible, **access reviews** to recertify, and swap broad roles (Owner, Contributor) for narrow or custom ones. Prefer **groups** over direct user assignments.

**Soft delete** (14 days default, up to 180, always-on option), **immutable vault** (blocks operations that would lose recovery points; can be **locked**), and **multi-user authorization** with a **Resource Guard** owned by a different admin.

cards.front: Security controls with infrastructure as code?
cards.back: Define controls in **Bicep, ARM templates or Terraform** (policy assignments, role assignments, locks, Defender plans) so every environment gets the same baseline. Add **what-if** and template scanning in the pipeline before deployment.

cards.front: Baseline hardening for a storage account?
cards.back: **Require secure transfer** (HTTPS), **minimum TLS 1.2**, **disallow anonymous blob access**, **disallow Shared Key** access (forces Microsoft Entra authorization), restrict **network access**, and limit **SAS** lifetime with a SAS expiration policy.

Account keys give **full access** and cannot be tied to a person. Disabling Shared Key means requests must use **Microsoft Entra ID** (RBAC data roles), which also blocks **account and service SAS**. User delegation SAS still works.

Set public network access to **selected networks**: **virtual network rules** (need a service endpoint), **IP rules** (public ranges only), **resource instance rules**, and the **trusted Microsoft services** exception. Or disable public access and use **private endpoints**.

Always encrypted at rest (AES-256). Choose **Microsoft-managed keys** or **customer-managed keys** in Key Vault/Managed HSM. **Infrastructure encryption** double-encrypts (set at creation). **Encryption scopes** give containers or blobs their own key.

cards.front: Data roles for blob access with Entra ID?
cards.back: **Storage Blob Data Reader**, **Contributor** and **Owner** (Owner also sets POSIX ACLs and ownership). Management roles such as Contributor do **not** grant blob data access by themselves.

Defined on a container, share, queue or table. A **service SAS** can point at one for its start, expiry and permissions. **Change or delete the policy to revoke** every SAS that uses it. Maximum **five** per container.

cards.front: Defender for Storage: what does it do?
cards.back: **Activity monitoring** (alerts on unusual access, exfiltration, suspicious IPs; no resource logs needed), **malware scanning** (**on-upload** and **on-demand**, Microsoft Defender Antivirus, priced per GB) and **sensitive data threat detection** (no extra cost).

A **monthly cap** on GB scanned per account, results as **blob index tags**, to **Event Grid** (automation) or **Log Analytics** (audit), and optional **soft delete of malicious blobs**. Hash reputation analysis is a lighter check that does not read the whole file.

**SQL authentication** (username and password in the database), **Microsoft Entra authentication** (users, groups, managed identities), or both. **Microsoft Entra-only authentication** turns SQL logins off. Set a **Microsoft Entra admin** on the server first.

**Server-level IP rules** apply to every database on the logical server. **Database-level IP rules** apply to one database. **Virtual network rules** allow a subnet. 'Allow Azure services' opens the server to all of Azure, so prefer **private endpoints** and deny public access.
Encrypts data files, logs and backups **at rest**, **on by default** for new databases. Uses a **service-managed key** or a **customer-managed key** in Key Vault. The app needs no changes.
Encrypts chosen **columns in the client driver**, so the data stays encrypted in use and **database admins cannot see plaintext**. Keys stay with the client (for example in Key Vault).

cards.front: Dynamic data masking and row-level security?
cards.back: **Dynamic data masking** hides part of a column in query results for non-privileged users; the stored data is unchanged, so it is not encryption. **Row-level security** filters which rows a user can read or change.

cards.front: Azure SQL auditing: destinations and scope?
cards.back: Writes database events to a **storage account**, a **Log Analytics workspace** or **Event Hubs**, in any combination. A **server-level** policy covers all existing and new databases. If both server and database auditing are on, events are audited twice. Prefer server-level.
Configured **per instance** with T-SQL or the portal: create a server audit to a storage container (URL), or send audit events through **diagnostic settings** to Log Analytics or Event Hubs.

Four plans: **Azure SQL databases**, **SQL servers on machines** (Azure, hybrid, multicloud), **open-source relational databases** (PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB) and **Azure Cosmos DB**. Gives **threat alerts** (SQL injection, brute force, anomalous access) and, for SQL, **vulnerability assessment**.

cards.front: NSG and ASG essentials for SC-500?
cards.back: NSG rules: priority **100-4096**, lowest first, **first match wins**, stateful. Inbound is checked at the **subnet NSG then the NIC NSG**. **ASGs** let rules target roles (web, db) instead of IPs. Defaults end in **DenyAllInbound 65500**.

cards.front: Azure Virtual Network Manager security admin rules?
cards.back: Central rules applied to **network groups** of virtual networks, **evaluated before NSGs**. Actions: **Allow** (NSGs still evaluate after), **Deny** (stops; NSGs cannot override) and **Always Allow** (stops; NSGs cannot block). Priority **1-4096**.

Rules live in **rule collections** inside a **security admin configuration**, which you **deploy** to regions. Only **one security admin configuration per region** (use several rule collections). Changes apply with a short delay (eventual consistency).

Turn a virtual hub into a **secured virtual hub** by adding **Azure Firewall** (or a supported security partner) and manage it with **Azure Firewall Manager**. **Routing intent** sends internet and private traffic through the hub's firewall.

**Site-to-site:** IPsec/IKE tunnels; use a **custom IPsec/IKE policy** for required algorithms. **Point-to-site:** authenticate with **Microsoft Entra ID** (supports Conditional Access and MFA), certificates or RADIUS, over OpenVPN or IKEv2.

Zero Trust network access to **private apps** without a VPN. Users run the **Global Secure Access client**; traffic reaches apps through **private network connectors** inside your network. Define apps with **Quick Access** or per-app segments and apply **Conditional Access** per app.

cards.front: Private endpoint vs Private Link service?
cards.back: **Private endpoint:** a NIC with a private IP in **your** VNet that connects to a PaaS resource (or to a Private Link service). **Private Link service:** **your own** service, behind a **Standard Load Balancer**, published so consumers connect with private endpoints; you approve connections.

cards.front: Azure Firewall SKUs and rule types?
cards.back: **Basic** (small sites, up to 250 Mbps; threat intelligence is **alert only**), **Standard** (threat intelligence **alert and deny**, DNS proxy, **web categories** by FQDN), **Premium** (adds **TLS inspection**, **IDPS**, full-path **URL filtering** and URL-based web categories). Rules: **DNAT**, **network**, **application**, managed in a **Firewall Policy**. Needs **AzureFirewallSubnet** and a UDR to steer traffic.

cards.front: Network Watcher tools for effective rules?
cards.back: **IP flow verify** (is this packet allowed, and by which rule), **NSG diagnostics** (also for ranges and service tags), **Effective security rules** (the combined rules on a NIC), **Next hop**, **Connection troubleshoot**. IP flow verify also checks **AVNM admin rules**.

cards.front: Finding overshared SharePoint data before Copilot uses it?
cards.back: Purview **Data Security Posture Management** runs a **data risk assessment every week for the top 100 SharePoint sites by usage**, with no setup. Add **custom assessments** for chosen sites. Results show overshared and unlabeled sensitive content with fixes (labels, restricting access).

cards.front: What does DSPM (for AI) give you?
cards.back: Insight into **AI activity** (Copilot, agents, third-party AI sites), **one-click policies** (DLP, collection, insider risk), **data risk assessments** and compliance controls. Needs **Purview Audit** on; third-party AI sites also need **onboarded devices** and the **Purview browser extension**. Allow about 24 hours for data.

cards.front: Real-time protection for Copilot Studio agents?
cards.back: Agents already block prompt injection (UPIA and XPIA) by default. Adding **Microsoft Defender** (or another provider) as the **external threat detection** system makes the agent ask it **before every tool invocation**; the system answers **allow or block**. Only for agents with **generative orchestration**.

cards.front: Microsoft Entra Agent ID: the objects?
cards.back: **Agent identity blueprint** (template; holds the credentials), **agent identity** (one per agent instance; no credentials of its own), optional **agent's user account**. Each needs a **sponsor** (business accountability) and should have an **owner** (technical admin).

cards.front: Conditional Access and governance for agent identities?
cards.back: Conditional Access can target **agent identities** and use **agent risk** from ID Protection. Apply policy at the **blueprint** so all its agents inherit it; **disabling a blueprint blocks all its agents**. Govern access with **access packages**; expiry notices go to the sponsor.

In the **incident graph**, select a node (for example a compromised agent or identity) and choose **View blast radius**: a graph of paths from that node to **critical assets**, up to a few hops, scoped to your permissions. Needs onboarding to the **Microsoft Sentinel data lake**. Use it to judge impact, then disable the agent identity or its blueprint.

Backed by **Azure API Management**, enabled from the Foundry portal for a Foundry resource. It sits between clients and model deployments and enforces **tokens-per-minute limits and token quotas per project**, plus content safety, logging and semantic caching. Over the TPM limit returns **429**; over quota returns **403**.

A Defender for Cloud workload protection plan giving **threat protection for AI services**: alerts on jailbreaks, data leakage, credential theft and more, using **Prompt Shields** and threat intelligence, shown in Defender XDR. Optional **user prompt evidence** adds prompt snippets to alerts.

A **guardrail** is a set of **controls**; each has a **risk**, **intervention points** and an **action**. Points: **user input, tool call, tool response, output** (the two tool points are agents only). An **agent's guardrail fully overrides its model's**. Agents support **Annotate and block** only.

cards.front: Data and AI security dashboard, and agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center?
cards.back: **Defender for Cloud's Data and AI security dashboard** shows data and AI resources, protection coverage, top alerts, recommendations and attack paths; full use needs **Defender CSPM** with sensitive data discovery. The **Microsoft 365 admin center** is where you see, approve, block and assign **agents** for Microsoft 365 users.

**Server-side encryption** is always on (platform-managed or customer-managed keys through a **disk encryption set**). **Encryption at host** also covers temp disks and caches end to end: use it for new VMs. **Azure Disk Encryption** (BitLocker/DM-Crypt) **retires 15 Sept 2028**. **Confidential disk encryption** binds keys to the VM's TPM.

Managed RDP/SSH over **TLS 443** with **no public IP on the VMs**. Needs **AzureBastionSubnet (/26 or larger)** and a Standard public IP. **Basic**, **Standard** (native client, file transfer, shareable links, scaling) and **Premium** (**session recording**, private-only). Reaches peered VNets.

Part of **Defender for Servers Plan 2**. Management ports stay **closed**; an authorized user **requests access** for a port, source IP and limited time, and Defender for Cloud adds a temporary allow rule to the **NSG or Azure Firewall**, then removes it.

Installs the **Connected Machine agent** on on-premises, AWS or GCP servers so they appear as Azure resources. Then you can apply **Azure Policy and Machine Configuration**, **Defender for Servers**, Azure Monitor and Update Manager to them.

cards.front: Defender for Servers Plan 1 vs Plan 2?
cards.back: **P1:** Defender for Endpoint **EDR** plus core vulnerability management. **P2:** all of P1 plus **agentless scanning**, **JIT VM access**, **file integrity monitoring**, **premium Defender Vulnerability Management**, OS configuration assessment, regulatory compliance and a **500 MB per machine daily ingestion benefit**.

cards.front: Onboarding hybrid and multicloud servers to Defender for Servers?
cards.back: On-premises: onboard with **Azure Arc**. AWS and GCP: create a **connector** in Defender for Cloud, which onboards machines through Arc. The **Defender for Endpoint extension** is then installed automatically on supported machines.

Takes **disk snapshots** and analyzes them out of band, with **no agent and no performance impact**. Finds **vulnerabilities, secrets and malware** and builds software inventory. Included with **Defender for Servers P2** or **Defender CSPM**; on by default with P2. You can exclude machines.

Security type **Trusted launch** (the default for Gen2 VMs) gives **Secure Boot** (only signed boot components), **vTPM** (measured boot and key storage) and **boot integrity monitoring** through attestation. Other security types: **Standard** and **Confidential VMs**.

Formerly Guest Configuration. **Audits or enforces settings inside the OS** (password policy, security baselines, installed software) through **Azure Policy**. Needs the **Machine Configuration extension** and a **system-assigned managed identity**; works on Azure VMs and **Arc-enabled servers**.

cards.front: Defender for Containers: what does it cover?
cards.back: **Posture** (agentless discovery of clusters, misconfiguration recommendations), **vulnerability assessment** of container images in registries and running workloads, and **runtime threat protection** through the **Defender sensor** on nodes plus control-plane audit logs. Works for AKS, and for EKS and GKE through connectors.

Integrate with **Microsoft Entra ID**, use **Azure RBAC for Kubernetes authorization**, and **disable local accounts**. Protect the API server with a **private cluster** or **authorized IP ranges**. Give pods identity with **Microsoft Entra Workload ID**.

**Network policies** restrict pod-to-pod traffic. **Azure Policy for Kubernetes** audits or denies risky pod settings (privileged containers, host paths). Pull secrets from **Key Vault** with the Secrets Store CSI driver. Keep node images and Kubernetes versions patched.

**Disable the admin user**; pull with a **managed identity** and **AcrPull**. **Premium** adds **private endpoints** and more. Restrict public network access, and let Defender for Containers scan images for vulnerabilities.

Use **managed identities** instead of stored credentials, deploy into a **virtual network**, keep **secrets** in Key Vault references, and limit **ingress** (Container Apps: internal-only ingress, IP restrictions, built-in authentication).

cards.front: Azure Functions: authentication and network access?
cards.back: **Function keys** are shared secrets, fine for simple callers. For real identity use **App Service Authentication (Easy Auth)** with Microsoft Entra ID. Network: **access restrictions**, **private endpoints** (inbound) and **VNet integration** (outbound).

Request triggers are protected by a **SAS signature in the URL**; add **Microsoft Entra OAuth** policies and **IP restrictions**. Turn on **secure inputs and outputs** to hide data in run history. Connect to other services with a **managed identity**.

**HTTPS Only**, **minimum TLS version**, **managed identity**, **Key Vault references** for app settings, **built-in authentication**, **access restrictions** and **private endpoints**; turn off FTP and basic-auth publishing.

Runs on **Application Gateway**, **Front Door** (and Azure CDN). **Managed rule sets** (OWASP-based, bot protection) plus **custom rules** (IP, geo, rate limit). **Detection mode** only logs; **Prevention mode** blocks. Use **exclusions** to fix false positives.

cards.front: Protecting back-end APIs with API Management?
cards.back: Policies: **validate-jwt** / validate-azure-ad-token (check tokens), **rate-limit** and **quota** (throttle), **ip-filter**, subscription keys. Authenticate to back ends with a **managed identity** or client certificate. **Defender for APIs** adds inventory, posture and threat detection.

**Foundational CSPM (free):** recommendations, secure score, MCSB. **Defender CSPM (paid):** adds **attack path analysis**, **cloud security explorer**, **agentless scanning**, **data security posture** (sensitive data discovery), **governance rules** and risk prioritization.

cards.front: Attack path analysis and cloud security explorer?
cards.back: **Attack paths** show chains an attacker could follow from an exposed entry point to a valuable target (for example internet-exposed VM → vulnerable → has permission to a Key Vault). **Cloud security explorer** lets you query the same graph yourself.

Paid plans enabled **per subscription** (some per resource): **Servers, Containers, Storage, Databases, App Service, Key Vault, Resource Manager, APIs, AI Services**. They raise **security alerts**. Turn on with Environment settings or at scale with **Azure Policy**.

Add a **connector** under Environment settings. **AWS:** deploy the generated **CloudFormation** template (management account or single account). **GCP:** run the generated script in Cloud Shell (organization or project). Servers come in through **Azure Arc**. CSPM is agentless.

The **regulatory compliance dashboard** scores controls for assigned standards across Azure, AWS and GCP. MCSB is default; add standards per subscription or connector, or build **custom standards** and recommendations.

cards.front: Defender Vulnerability Management for Azure VMs?
cards.back: The built-in vulnerability scanner for Defender for Servers. **Agent-based** (Defender for Endpoint sensor, P1 and P2) and **agentless** (P2). Findings appear as recommendations with CVEs and software inventory. BYOL scanners are the alternative.

Maps your **internet-facing assets from the outside**: domains, IP blocks, hosts, email contacts, ASNs, Whois organizations. Starts from **discovery seeds** and follows connections with **no agents or credentials**, exposing unknown ('shadow') assets and their vulnerabilities. An EASM view is **included in Defender CSPM**.

A percentage from the MCSB recommendations. Each **control** has a maximum score; you earn it only when **all** its recommendations are fixed for a resource. Exempting a resource removes it from the calculation.

Sentinel is enabled on a **Log Analytics workspace**. One workspace is simplest; use more for data residency or separate tenants. Onboard the workspace to the **Microsoft Defender portal** for unified incidents; one workspace is **primary**.

**Reader** (view data, incidents, workbooks), **Responder** (Reader + manage incidents), **Contributor** (Responder + create and edit rules, workbooks, install solutions), **Playbook Operator** (list and run playbooks), **Automation Contributor** (for Sentinel's own account to run playbooks from automation rules; **not for users**). Assign at the **resource group**.

Where you install **solutions**: packages of data connectors, analytics rules, workbooks, hunting queries, parsers and playbooks for a product or scenario. Install, then **configure** the connector and enable the rule templates.

Use the **Syslog via AMA** and **Common Event Format via AMA** connectors: a **Linux log forwarder** with the **Azure Monitor Agent** and a **data collection rule**. Syslog lands in the **Syslog** table, CEF in **CommonSecurityLog**.

**Windows Security Events via AMA:** AMA on each machine plus a **DCR** choosing All, Common, Minimal or custom (XPath) events → **SecurityEvent** table. **Windows Forwarded Events:** AMA on a **Windows Event Collector** server that receives events by **WEF** → **WindowsEvent** table. Many built-in rules query **SecurityEvent**, so forwarded events may need adapted rules or ASIM parsers. Non-Azure machines need **Azure Arc** first.

Create a table ending in **_CL** and send data with the **Logs ingestion API** through a **data collection rule** (and endpoint), which can **transform** data with KQL at ingestion. Pick the table's tier: analytics or data lake.

**Automation rules** run on **incident created, incident updated or alert created**: assign owner, change severity or status, add tags or tasks, suppress, and **run playbooks**, in a set order. **Playbooks** are **Azure Logic Apps** workflows that act on other systems.

cards.front: Data tiers and retention in Sentinel?
cards.back: **Analytics tier:** hot data for rules, hunting and workbooks; Sentinel tables keep **90 days** at no extra retention charge, extendable to **2 years**. **Data lake tier:** low-cost storage with **total retention up to 12 years**; no real-time analytics rules; query with KQL jobs and notebooks.

cards.front: Querying Purview Audit in Defender XDR?
cards.back: Audit search is available from the **Defender portal** as well as the Purview portal. In **advanced hunting**, Microsoft 365 audit activity is in **CloudAppEvents** (needs the Microsoft 365 app connector in Defender for Cloud Apps). You need audit read permissions.

cards.front: What is a Security Compute Unit (SCU)?
cards.back: The unit of capacity that runs Security Copilot workloads, in the standalone portal, embedded experiences and **agents**. Capacity is an **Azure resource** attached to a **workspace**. Microsoft 365 E5 includes a monthly SCU allowance.

A **workspace** is a scoped, tenant-bound environment where users, plugins, promptbooks and agents operate, with its own **capacity** and role assignments. Auto-provisioned tenants get a **default workspace**.

**Owner** and **Contributor**. They are **not Entra roles** and give access to the **platform only**, never to security data. **Owners** manage capacity, plugins, role assignment, data sharing and file upload settings. **Contributors** create sessions and use Copilot. At least **two owners** are always kept.

cards.front: Who gets the roles by default?
cards.back: Certain Entra roles **inherit Owner** (Global Administrator, Security Administrator and a few others). Contributor defaults to the **Recommended Microsoft Security roles** group; the older **Everyone** default should be removed. Best practice: assign roles to a **security group**.

cards.front: Why can a Contributor still see no data?
cards.back: Copilot acts **on behalf of the user**. Each plugin needs the user's own role in that product: for example **Microsoft Sentinel Reader** for the Sentinel plugin, an **Intune** role for Intune. Copilot never goes beyond the user's access.

Connect Copilot to data and tools: **Microsoft** plugins (Defender XDR, Sentinel, Entra, Intune, Purview…), **non-Microsoft** plugins and **custom** plugins. Turn them on under **Manage sources**; some need extra setup. Owners control **who can add and manage custom plugins**.

Agents run tasks with a configured **identity, triggers and permissions**. Find **Microsoft agents** in the agent library and **partner agents** in the **Security Store**; after setup they appear under **Active agents**. Running agents **uses SCUs**. Store subscriptions are billed separately.

cards.front: Provisioning capacity: who can do it?
cards.back: You need **Azure Owner or Contributor** on the subscription or resource group (capacity is an Azure resource) and **Security Administrator** or higher in the tenant.

questions.q: Admins must hold the Security Administrator role only when they need it, after approval, for at most four hours. What should you configure?
opts: An eligible assignment in Privileged Identity Management with approval required
A Conditional Access policy that blocks the role
A dynamic group with the role
questions.why: Eligible PIM assignments are activated just in time, with approval and a time limit.

questions.q: You are about to enforce MFA for all users with Conditional Access. What should you do first to avoid locking out the tenant?
opts: Exclude the emergency access accounts and run the policy in report-only mode
Assign the policy to Global Administrators only
Delete legacy authentication protocols from the tenant
Disable security defaults and all other policies
questions.why: Break-glass accounts are excluded, and report-only shows the impact before enforcement.

questions.q: A daemon service with no signed-in user must read all users' mailboxes through Microsoft Graph. Which permission type is needed?
questions.why: With no user present the app acts as itself, which needs application permissions and admin consent.

questions.q: Which TWO authentication methods are phishing-resistant?
questions.why: FIDO2 passkeys and Windows Hello for Business are bound to the device and origin. SMS and voice can be intercepted or phished.

questions.q: For each statement, select Yes if it is true. Otherwise, select No.
stmts: An application permission can be granted by any user through user consent.
A user-assigned managed identity can be attached to more than one Azure resource.
PIM can require MFA when a user activates a role.
questions.why: Application permissions always need admin consent. User-assigned identities are shareable. PIM activation settings include MFA.

questions.q: Match each need to the Entra feature.
rows: Just-in-time admin roles
Require a compliant device for an app
Let users ask an admin to approve an app
VM reads Key Vault with no stored secret
questions.why: One feature per job.

questions.q: Where do you restrict which users may sign in to a SaaS app that is integrated with Entra ID?
opts: On the app registration's redirect URIs
In the tenant's custom domain settings
On the enterprise application (service principal): require assignment and assign users
questions.why: User assignment and sign-in controls live on the enterprise application.

questions.q: Users keep approving risky third-party apps. You want them to request approval instead of granting consent themselves. What should you configure?
opts: Restrict user consent and enable the admin consent workflow
Grant tenant-wide admin consent to all apps
Make all users Cloud Application Administrators
questions.why: Limiting user consent stops the risky grants, and the workflow routes requests to reviewers.

questions.q: An app's managed identity must read secret values from one vault and nothing else. Which role should you assign?
questions.why: Secrets User reads secret contents. Reader sees metadata only. Officer can also create and delete.

questions.q: You must make sure no one, including a subscription Owner, can permanently delete keys in a vault before 90 days pass. What should you enable?
questions.why: Purge protection blocks purging until the retention period ends and cannot be turned off.

questions.q: A storage account uses a customer-managed key. The vault firewall blocks public access. What lets the storage service reach the vault?
opts: Allow trusted Microsoft services to bypass the firewall, plus key permissions for the storage identity
Granting Key Vault Reader to all users
A user-defined route to the vault
questions.why: The trusted services exception covers network access. The service identity still needs data-plane permission.

questions.q: Which TWO statements about Key Vault soft delete are true?
opts: It cannot be disabled once on
The retention period cannot be changed after the vault is created
questions.why: Soft delete is permanent, 7 to 90 days (default 90), fixed at creation, and covers vaults, keys, secrets and certificates.

questions.q: For each statement, select Yes if it is true. Otherwise, select No.
stmts: Key Vault Reader can read the value of a secret.
Premium tier is needed for HSM-protected keys.
A user with Contributor on the vault can read secrets when the vault uses Azure RBAC, without any data-plane role.
questions.why: Reader sees metadata. Premium adds HSM keys. With RBAC, data access needs a data-plane role.

questions.q: Match each task to the least-privileged Key Vault role.
rows: Read a secret value
Create and delete secrets
Encrypt and decrypt with a key
Permanently delete a soft-deleted vault
questions.why: User roles use objects. Officer roles manage them.

questions.q: Defender for Cloud shows an attack path where an internet-exposed VM holds a plaintext storage key. Which capability found the key?
opts: Agentless secrets scanning in Defender CSPM
questions.why: Agentless secrets scanning inspects machine disks for secrets and feeds attack path analysis.

questions.q: You need an alert when a vault is accessed from a Tor exit node. What should you enable?
questions.why: Defender for Key Vault detects unusual and suspicious access patterns.

questions.q: A backup admin's account is compromised. You need a second person, in another team, to approve disabling soft delete or reducing retention on the vault. What should you configure?
opts: Multi-user authorization with a Resource Guard
A custom RBAC role with NotActions
questions.why: A Resource Guard owned by someone else gates critical vault operations.

questions.q: You must show auditors how your subscriptions measure against PCI DSS. What should you do in Defender for Cloud?
opts: Add the PCI DSS standard and review the regulatory compliance dashboard
questions.why: The dashboard maps assessments to each standard's controls.

questions.q: A custom role lists Actions: Microsoft.Compute/* and NotActions: Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/delete. A user also has Contributor on the same scope. Can the user delete VMs?
opts: Yes, because NotActions is not a deny and Contributor grants delete
No, NotActions always blocks the action
No, custom roles override built-in roles
questions.why: NotActions only subtracts within that role. Another assignment can still grant the action.

questions.q: You need to stop anyone from deploying storage accounts that allow public blob access, across all subscriptions. What should you use?
opts: A resource lock on each subscription
An Azure Policy assignment with the Deny effect at the management group
questions.why: Deny blocks non-compliant deployments, and management group scope covers every subscription under it.

questions.q: Which TWO help reduce standing privileged access?
opts: Convert active role assignments to eligible in PIM
Share one admin account between the team
Run access reviews on privileged roles
Assign Owner at the root management group
questions.why: PIM removes standing access. Reviews remove what is no longer needed.

questions.q: For each statement, select Yes if it is true. Otherwise, select No.
stmts: The Microsoft cloud security benchmark is assigned by default in Defender for Cloud.
A locked immutable vault's immutability setting can be turned off later.
Custom Microsoft Entra roles require Entra ID P1.
questions.why: MCSB is the default standard. Locking immutability is irreversible. Custom Entra roles need P1.

questions.q: Match each requirement to the control.
rows: Block resources outside approved regions
Protect recovery points from deletion
Stop accidental deletion of a resource group
Same security baseline in every environment
questions.why: Policy shapes, vaults keep, locks protect, IaC repeats.

questions.q: A team needs to restart VMs and read their metrics, nothing more. No built-in role fits. What should you create?
opts: A custom Azure role with only those Actions and the needed AssignableScopes
questions.why: Custom Azure roles grant exactly the management-plane actions you list.

questions.q: All access to a storage account must be authorized with Microsoft Entra ID so that every request maps to an identity. What should you configure?
opts: Set the default tier to Cool
questions.why: With Shared Key off, account keys and key-signed SAS stop working, leaving Entra authorization.

questions.q: A web app lets customers upload files to Blob Storage. Files must be checked for malware as they arrive, and bad ones handled automatically. What should you enable?
opts: Defender for Storage on-upload malware scanning with results sent to Event Grid
questions.why: On-upload scanning checks each blob, and Event Grid lets a function or logic app quarantine it.

questions.q: A user with the Contributor role on a storage account gets 403 when listing blobs with Entra authorization in the portal. Why?
opts: The user needs the Reader role as well
Contributor is a management role; a Storage Blob Data role is needed
questions.why: Data-plane access needs a data role such as Storage Blob Data Reader.

questions.q: Which TWO settings reduce the risk of data being read anonymously or over an insecure channel?
questions.why: One blocks public containers, the other forces HTTPS.

questions.q: For each statement, select Yes if it is true. Otherwise, select No.
stmts: Defender for Storage activity monitoring needs diagnostic resource logs to be enabled first.
A stored access policy can revoke the service SAS tokens that reference it.
IP network rules can allow a private address range such as 10.0.0.0/24.
questions.why: Activity monitoring needs no resource logs. Policies revoke linked SAS. IP rules take public ranges only.

questions.q: Match each goal to the storage feature.
rows: Detect a malicious file as it is uploaded
Use your own key in Key Vault
Reach the account on a private IP
Revoke a set of SAS tokens at once
questions.why: Detect, encrypt, isolate, revoke.

questions.q: You need to keep malware scanning costs predictable on a high-traffic account. What should you set?
opts: A monthly cap on GB scanned
questions.why: The cap stops scanning for the month when reached, and alerts warn at 75% and 100%.

questions.q: Different containers in one account must be encrypted with different keys. What should you use?
questions.why: An encryption scope assigns its own key to a container or blob.

questions.q: Security policy says no SQL logins may exist; only identities from the directory may connect to Azure SQL Database. What should you enable?
questions.why: Entra-only authentication disables SQL authentication for the server.

questions.q: Database administrators must not be able to read the credit card column, even when querying the table directly. What should you use?
questions.why: Always Encrypted keeps data encrypted from the client, so the server and DBAs never see plaintext. Masking can be bypassed by privileged users.

questions.q: You need one audit configuration that covers every database on a logical server, including databases created later, queryable with KQL. What should you configure?
opts: Database-level auditing on each database to a storage account
A resource lock on the server
Server-level auditing to a Log Analytics workspace
questions.why: Server-level auditing applies to all databases, and Log Analytics supports KQL.

questions.q: Help desk staff should see only the last four digits of phone numbers in query results. The stored values must not change. What should you configure?
questions.why: Masking changes what non-privileged users see, not what is stored.

questions.q: Which TWO are plans within Defender for Databases?
questions.why: The four database plans are Azure SQL, SQL servers on machines, open-source relational, and Cosmos DB.

questions.q: For each statement, select Yes if it is true. Otherwise, select No.
stmts: TDE protects data from a database administrator running SELECT statements.
A server-level firewall rule applies to all databases on the logical server.
Auditing can write to a storage account and a Log Analytics workspace at the same time.
questions.why: TDE is encryption at rest only. Server rules cover all databases. Destinations can be combined.

questions.q: Match each requirement to the SQL feature.
rows: Encrypt files and backups at rest
Hide column values from DBAs
Each sales rep sees only their own rows
Record who ran which statements
questions.why: At rest, in use, per row, on record.

questions.q: Defender for Cloud should alert on a possible SQL injection against SQL Server running on Azure VMs and on-premises servers. Which plan should you enable?
opts: Defender for SQL servers on machines
questions.why: SQL Server on VMs and Arc-enabled servers is covered by the SQL servers on machines plan.

questions.q: The central security team must block inbound SSH from the internet in every virtual network, and application teams must not be able to override it with their NSGs. What should you use?
opts: An Azure Virtual Network Manager security admin rule with the Deny action
An NSG rule with priority 100 in each subnet
questions.why: Admin Deny rules are evaluated before NSGs and cannot be overridden by them.

questions.q: An AVNM security admin rule uses the Allow action for TCP 443. A subnet NSG denies TCP 443. What happens to the traffic?
opts: It is allowed, because admin rules win
It is allowed only for 60 seconds
It is denied by the NSG
questions.why: Allow passes the traffic on to NSG evaluation. Only Always Allow skips the NSG.

questions.q: Remote users need access to an internal web app without a VPN, with per-app Conditional Access. What should you deploy?
opts: Microsoft Entra Private Access with a private network connector
questions.why: Private Access is ZTNA for private apps through connectors and the Global Secure Access client.

questions.q: You must inspect outbound HTTPS traffic for malware and use signature-based intrusion detection and prevention. Which Azure Firewall SKU is required?
questions.why: TLS inspection and IDPS are Premium features.

questions.q: A small branch firewall must block, not just log, traffic to known malicious IPs and domains, and allow web categories. What is the lowest Azure Firewall SKU that does this?
questions.why: Basic threat intelligence is alert only and has no web categories. Standard adds deny mode and FQDN-based web categories.

questions.q: Your team hosts an API on VMs behind a Standard Load Balancer and wants customers in other tenants to reach it privately from their own VNets. What should you create?
opts: A VNet peering to each customer
questions.why: A Private Link service publishes your service so consumers create private endpoints to it.

questions.q: Which TWO authentication options are available for point-to-site VPN users?
questions.why: P2S supports Entra ID, certificate and RADIUS authentication.

questions.q: For each statement, select Yes if it is true. Otherwise, select No.
stmts: Only one security admin configuration can be deployed to a region per network manager.
An Always Allow admin rule can be blocked by a subnet NSG.
A secured virtual hub is a Virtual WAN hub with Azure Firewall or a security partner.
questions.why: One config per region. Always Allow ends evaluation. Secured hubs add a firewall.

questions.q: Match each Azure Firewall rule type to its job.
rows: Publish an internal server on a public IP and port
Allow by IP, port and protocol
Allow outbound by FQDN
Block known malicious IPs and domains
questions.why: Translate, filter by L3/L4, filter by name, block by intel.

questions.q: A VM cannot receive traffic on port 8080. You need to know which rule denies it, including any Virtual Network Manager admin rules. Which tool should you use?
questions.why: IP flow verify returns allowed or denied and the rule, checking NSGs and AVNM admin rules.

questions.q: Before rolling out Microsoft 365 Copilot you must find SharePoint sites where sensitive files are shared too widely. What should you review first?
opts: The default data risk assessment in Purview Data Security Posture Management
The Defender for Cloud secure score
questions.why: DSPM assesses the top 100 SharePoint sites weekly for oversharing without any setup.

questions.q: A Copilot Studio agent must have each planned tool call checked by your security platform, which can block it before it runs. What should you configure?
opts: A Foundry guardrail on the agent's model
An NSG on the agent's subnet
External threat detection with Microsoft Defender as the provider
questions.why: The agent calls the threat detection endpoint before invoking each tool and follows its allow or block decision.

questions.q: All agents created from one blueprint must be blocked from signing in when their risk is high. Where should you apply the Conditional Access policy?
questions.why: Policies applied at the blueprint are inherited by every agent identity created from it.

questions.q: Several teams share one Foundry resource. One project must not consume more than a set number of tokens per minute. What should you configure?
opts: AI Gateway with a token limit for the project
A guardrail with the Violence risk
questions.why: AI Gateway enforces TPM limits and token quotas at the project level.

questions.q: An agent in Foundry reads web pages through a tool. You must stop hidden instructions in a page from steering the agent. Which control fits?
opts: A Hate control at user input
A protected material control at output
A token quota in AI Gateway
An indirect attack control at the tool response intervention point
questions.why: Indirect prompt injection arrives in tool responses, so scan and block there.

questions.q: Which TWO are needed for DSPM to report on users' activity with third-party AI websites?
questions.why: Third-party AI site insights depend on onboarded devices and the browser extension.

questions.q: For each statement, select Yes if it is true. Otherwise, select No.
stmts: An agent identity stores its own client secret.
If an agent has its own guardrail, the model's guardrail still applies as well.
Defender for AI Services alerts appear in the Defender XDR portal.
questions.why: Credentials sit on the blueprint. The agent guardrail fully overrides the model's. AI alerts integrate with Defender XDR.

questions.q: Match each task to the tool.
rows: Find overshared SharePoint content
Alert on a jailbreak attempt against a model
Cap tokens per project
Approve or block agents for Microsoft 365 users
questions.why: Data posture, threat alerts, traffic control, admin control.

questions.q: Every agent identity must have someone accountable for deciding whether the agent is still needed. Which role is that?
questions.why: The sponsor carries business accountability. The owner handles technical operations.

questions.q: RDP on production VMs must be closed by default and opened only on request, for a limited time and from the requester's IP. What should you enable?
opts: Just-in-time VM access in Defender for Servers Plan 2
A permanent NSG allow rule for the corporate range
questions.why: JIT keeps ports closed and adds time-limited rules on approved requests.

questions.q: You must scan VMs for vulnerabilities and exposed secrets without installing anything on them or affecting performance. What should you use?
opts: The Defender for Endpoint sensor only
questions.why: Agentless scanning analyzes disk snapshots outside the VM.

questions.q: On-premises Windows servers must be protected by Defender for Servers and governed with Azure Policy. What must you do first?
opts: Onboard the servers to Azure Arc
questions.why: Arc makes the servers Azure resources so Defender and Policy can reach them.

questions.q: Compliance requires recording all administrator RDP sessions to VMs that have no public IP. Which Bastion SKU do you need?
questions.why: Session recording is a Premium feature.

questions.q: Which TWO features are part of Trusted launch?
questions.why: Trusted launch combines Secure Boot, vTPM and boot integrity monitoring.

questions.q: For each statement, select Yes if it is true. Otherwise, select No.
stmts: Defender for Servers Plan 1 includes just-in-time VM access.
Azure Machine Configuration can apply to Arc-enabled servers.
Azure Disk Encryption is the recommended option for new VMs.
questions.why: JIT is Plan 2. Machine Configuration covers Arc servers. ADE is retiring; use encryption at host.

questions.q: Match each requirement to the feature.
rows: Enforce a password policy inside the OS
Detect changes to system files and registry
Encrypt temp disks and caches end to end
Block unsigned bootloaders
questions.why: In-guest policy, change detection, host encryption, boot trust.

questions.q: Which Defender for Servers plan do you need for file integrity monitoring and premium vulnerability management capabilities?
questions.why: Both are Plan 2 features.

questions.q: A new WAF policy on Application Gateway must be tested against production traffic without blocking any requests. Which mode should you use?
questions.why: Detection mode logs matches only. Prevention blocks them.

questions.q: Developers currently use a cluster admin certificate to reach AKS. You must make all access go through directory identities and roles. Which TWO should you configure?
opts: Microsoft Entra integration with Azure RBAC for Kubernetes
Open the API server to all IP addresses
